title: How to build a long-term investing plan using ETFs only
description: The 'Boglehead' blueprint for a simple, low-cost, million-dollar portfolio.
content:
You do not need to own individual stocks to get rich. In fact, owning individual stocks increases your risk of failure. The most reliable path to wealth is the **ETF-Only Portfolio**. By using broad-market Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), you can own the entire global economy for pennies. This strategy, popularized by John Bogle and the FIRE movement, requires almost zero maintenance and beats the vast majority of professional hedge funds over a 20-year timeline. This guide shows you exactly which tickers to buy to build a 'Set and Forget' fortune.

Key Takeaways

  • The 3-Fund Portfolio: The classic structure: Total US Stock Market + Total International Stock Market + Total Bond Market. That's it.
  • No Single Point of Failure: If one company (like Enron) goes to zero, your ETF portfolio barely moves. You are diversified against disaster.
  • Rock-Bottom Fees: An ETF portfolio costs ~0.05% per year. An active mutual fund costs ~0.80%. You save thousands in fees.
  • Tax Efficiency: ETFs are structured to minimize capital gains taxes, making them ideal for taxable brokerage accounts.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US investors are spoiled with choices. Vanguard, Fidelity, and Schwab offer competing ETFs that are virtually identical. Whether you buy VTI, ITOT, or SCHB, you are buying the same thing: The US Economy.

The Ingredients

Build your portfolio with these LEGO blocks.

Block 1: US Equities (The Engine)

Tickers: VTI (Vanguard Total Market), ITOT (iShares Total Market).

Allocation: 50% - 60%.

Why: Captures the growth of Apple, Amazon, and 3,500 other US companies.

Block 2: International Equities (The Hedge)

Tickers: VXUS (Vanguard Total Intl), IXUS (iShares Core Intl).

Allocation: 20% - 30%.

Why: Winners rotate. In the 2000s, International beat US. In the 2010s, US beat International. Owning both ensures you always own the winner.

Block 3: Bonds (The Safety)

Tickers: BND (Total Bond), AGG (Aggregate Bond).

Allocation: 10% - 20% (Adjust by Age).

Why: Reduces volatility. Allows you to sleep when stocks crash.

The Annual Maintenance Plan

  1. Buy Monthly: Automate your contributions. Do not look at the price. Just buy.
  2. Rebalance Annually: Once a year, check your percentages. If US Stocks grew to 70% (target 60%), sell the excess and buy more International/Bonds. This forces you to 'Sell High and Buy Low'.
  3. Ignore the News: Headlines about 'Market Crash' or 'Next Big Stock' are noise. Your ETF portfolio owns the market. You will participate in all growth automatically.
  4. Stay the Course: The only way to lose is to sell during a downturn. An ETF portfolio will recover. An individual stock might not.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why not just S&P 500 (VOO)?

VOO is great, but VTI includes Small and Mid-cap stocks too. VTI is more diversified. But honestly, VTI and VOO perform 99% identically. Pick either.

Do ETFs pay dividends?

Yes. Quarterly. Set your broker to 'Reinvest Dividends' (DRIP) to compound your growth automatically.

Can I retire on this?

Yes. This is how most 401(k) millionaires are made. Simple, boring, consistent contributions to broad funds over 30 years.
